extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and authors preparing qualitative research manuscripts (particularly in health/global health) and peer-reviewers/editors evaluating such manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting standards for preparing and evaluating qualitative research manuscripts, covering title/abstract, introduction, methods (design, sampling, data collection/analysis), trustworthiness, ethics, results, discussion, conclusions, and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper’s title should captivate the reader and entail precisely the covered content, specifying the type of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the title clear and informative about study type and focus so readers immediately know what was done; aim to 'entail precisely the covered content'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should encapsulate key research elements such as background, introduction, purpose, methodology, results, and conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a structured summary including background, objectives, methods, main results, and conclusions so the abstract accurately reflects the paper's content and facilitates indexing and quick appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: aim, rationale, and research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the aim of the study embedded within the introduction, provide rationale/justification, clearly state the research problem and articulate the research question and its relevance and connection to existing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify target audience in the introduction where appropriate; ensure alignment between research question, objectives, and methodology. For a ~3500-word paper, consider concise 3–4 paragraphs for the introduction (per Blignault & Ritchie).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: research design and theoretical framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear description of the research design and/or outline the study’s theoretical framework so readers understand the overall approach and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize the research design (what was done) and justify choice of theoretical framework; explain how the theory informed study design, data collection and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify the chosen methodology with respect to its suitability for addressing the research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why methods were appropriate for the research question and objectives; document trade-offs or limitations in methodological choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed description of the study population, sampling technique, study site, inclusion and exclusion criteria, sample characteristics, and recruitment strategy aligned with research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about participant selection and recruitment, including how triangulation was used in selection where applicable; provide enough contextual detail to judge transferability while considering confidentiality concerns in sensitive contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify data collection techniques and methods (e.g., interviews, focus groups, surveys, field notes), whether tools were pretested for validity/reliability, and the mode of contact (email, phone, face-to-face).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report interview guides (open/closed), criteria for data saturation, interview duration and timing, and whether interviews were repeated. Distinguish the depth and limitations of individual interviews vs focus groups and note researcher roles in data collection (e.g., multiple researchers required for focus groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription and data preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the transcription process of collected data and how raw data were prepared for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who transcribed, transcription conventions, whether transcripts were checked against recordings, and any steps taken to anonymize or secure transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis: coding and theme development
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how themes were generated, coding procedures, coding tree, the software used, involvement of data coders, and strategies for intercoder reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent stepwise description of analytic procedures (how themes were derived), include coding frameworks or trees (or appendices), name software tools, report how coding disagreements were resolved and any procedures to ensure dependability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant checking and triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report procedures such as participant checking (member checking), feedback, and data triangulation used to strengthen findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether and how findings/analyses were discussed with participants or peers, and how triangulation across data sources/methods was achieved; note debates about member checking (some guidance suggests benefits; others caution about challenges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to methodology during study
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and justify any changes made in the methodology during the research process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document deviations from protocol or emergent methodological decisions and provide rationale to allow readers to follow the decision trail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflexivity and researcher characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on researchers’ backgrounds, biases, perspectives, and their potential impact on the research process and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state researcher positions and how these influenced design, data collection, analysis and interpretation; include reflexive statements to enhance transparency and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting guidelines/checklist selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention specific reporting guidelines or standards (e.g., SRQR, COREQ, IMPAD-22) and ideally select a checklist before writing the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which guideline/checklist was used and where items are addressed; selecting a checklist pre-writing improves structure and reduces post-submission adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness and rigor (terminology and concepts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess quality using qualitative concepts such as credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability rather than quantitative terms 'validity' and 'reliability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each aspect of trustworthiness was addressed (e.g., credibility via member checking, dependability via audit trail) and provide evidence of rigorous analytic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use procedures such as member checking and peer discussion to attain credibility of interpretations and methodological approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who checked findings (participants, peers), what was checked, and outcomes of such checks; if member checking not used, justify why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of analysis and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain transparency, clarity and a strong foundation in detailing procedures, decisions and justifications so readers can track events and the logic leading to findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present analytic steps and examples showing how interpretations were made; provide audit trails, coding matrices or appendices where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval and informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ethical approval from the relevant authority and how ethical clearance was obtained; document informed consent procedures (oral or written).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the approving body, reference number if available, steps taken to obtain consent, and procedures for documenting committee decisions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data anonymity, confidentiality and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure and report measures for data anonymity, participant consent, confidentiality protections, and data security/anonymization procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how identities were protected, data storage/security measures, and any steps to redact or obscure identifying details—especially important in sensitive research and small samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: reporting findings and themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state what researchers found, establish major and minor themes, and present themes/concepts derived from analysis supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about quantity and quality of information; avoid dumping all data. Use quotations to illustrate findings—short quotes in the body, longer quotes in separate paragraphs—and align interpretations with the supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and wording of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Use careful wording and language to accurately convey results and their interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating claims; ensure interpretations do not go beyond the supporting data; present nuances and uncertainties where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: linking, interpretation, and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Link findings to established literature and theoretical/conceptual frameworks, present alternative explanations, compare with prior work, and discuss implications, transferability and contributions to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how findings fit with or challenge existing theory and evidence, explain the extent and limitations of results, and articulate potential implications for practice, policy, and future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Address potential biases in the study and their likely impact, and report them where appropriate (some guidelines place bias in results vs discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss forms of bias (selection, analytic, publication) and how they were considered or mitigated; follow guideline-recommended placement (ENTREQ vs PRISMA/MOOSE differences noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions: big-picture and relation to analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on the big picture in the conclusion, draw implications for the research field or future research, and ensure conclusions relate to the analysis/interpretation of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid introducing unfounded claims; relate conclusions back to evidence and discuss reflexivity as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the study’s strengths and candidly report limitations (e.g., small sample), documenting how data/analysis quality may affect conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how strengths support credibility and how limitations might undermine findings; document unexpected findings and validate them in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include recommendations that authentically derive from the findings, detailing implications for policy, practice and areas needing further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recommendations are grounded in results rather than wishful thinking; specify actionable or research-focused next steps tied to study evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and other support disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose sources of funding and any other support or assistance (including financial endorsement for authorship or publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funder names, nature of support, and any potential influence on study design, conduct or reporting; if names cannot be attached, provide complete descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and legal/copyright considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any potential conflicts of interest or biases that may have influenced the research and describe how they were managed; note copyright or legal rights where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about competing interests and steps taken to mitigate bias; include statements required by journal/publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comprehensive referencing to allow readers to locate sources used to justify methods and interpretations; include appendices (e.g., interview guides, coding trees) to enhance transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that key literature in the field is included and accurately presented; include supporting files (transcripts, guides, coding frameworks) where ethical and feasible.
